answers.question: A review found that the rule on the yes covers only changes the customer makes, and that a refund amount different from the proposal is checked only when the refund call answers, not when a later lookup shows the refund. Before: R-05 "When the customer changes any part of the proposal after the yes, the yes no longer counts and the agent proposes again." R-13 "When the refund call answers with an amount different from the one the customer said yes to, the agent makes no further change with the new amount, tells the customer the amount the refund call returned, and hands the case to staff as 'refund amount differs'." After: R-05 "Any change to the proposal after the yes voids the yes. When the customer changes any part of it, the agent proposes again." R-13 "When a refund call or a lookup shows a refund for an amount different from the one the customer said yes to, the agent makes no further change with the new amount, tells the customer the amount shown, and hands the case to staff as 'refund amount differs'." Do you accept these two changes?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.

answers.question: You said lookups may be retried on timeout without limit. Nothing then ends a lookup that keeps getting no answer, and the customer hears nothing while it runs. Shortest path: the customer asks to cancel, the lookup gets no answer, the agent looks again, again with no answer, and so on. Before: R-15 "When the first lookup of the customer's orders gets no answer, the agent tries it again; the owner set no limit on lookups." After: R-15 "When a lookup of the customer's orders gets no answer, the agent tries it again, up to 3 tries in all, telling the customer it is still looking. After the third try with no answer, it tells the customer it cannot look up their orders right now, and changes nothing." What ends repeated lookups?
answers.recommended: Yes: up to 3 tries in all, then the agent tells the customer it cannot look up their orders right now and changes nothing.
answers.reply: > Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: The rule for several orders says each gets its own proposal and yes, but not which goes first, or what happens when the customer names another order while a proposal waits for a yes. Before: R-14 "The agent works on one order at a time. A request to cancel another order gets its own proposal and its own yes." After: R-14 "The agent works on one order at a time, in the order the customer named them; each gets its own proposal and its own yes. When the customer names another order while a proposal waits for a yes, the agent asks whether they mean it instead of the first or as well. Instead: the earlier yes no longer counts and it proposes the new order. As well: it finishes the first order, then takes the second. After an order's case ends, a request to cancel another order starts again with a lookup." Do you accept this change?

Two rules read loosely. R-10 says the agent hands the case to staff when "the order is still not cancelled after the second cancel call", which could be read to include a second cancel call that answers "not cancellable" because the order shipped; that case is reported as shipped. R-12 points at other rules by number and adds words to the message you gave. Before: R-10 "The lookup fails, or the order is still not cancelled after the second cancel call: it says the outcome is unknown, issues no refund, and hands the case to staff as 'cancellation unknown'." R-12 "Each case R-08, R-09, R-10 and R-13 hand to staff gets a follow-up with its reason. When the follow-up call gets no answer, the agent tries once more; when that also gets no answer, it tells the customer what happened to the order and the refund, that it could not reach store staff, and to contact Harbor Goods support." After: R-10 "The lookup fails, or the lookup after the second cancel call still shows the order placed or processing: it says the outcome is unknown, issues no refund, and hands the case to staff as 'cancellation unknown'." R-12 "Each case handed to staff gets a follow-up with its reason: a refund that failed or was not issued, a refund whose status is unknown, a cancellation whose outcome is unknown, and a refund amount that differs. When the follow-up call gets no answer, the agent tries once more; when that also gets no answer, it tells the customer what happened to the order and the refund, and to contact Harbor Goods support." Do you accept these two changes?
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Shipped, report it and issue no refund.
> Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
